title: The Banana — crashed top shot: dedicated overhead-angle puppets (approved pose sheet)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Camera-angle puppets: for the overhead crash shot the show did NOT rotate the stock puppets — it built dedicated GB209_*_CRASHED_TOP_SHOT puppets (187 + 149 kf) with their own eye comps, drawn already-flattened from above, bruises and all. The SWF is the approved pose sheet on the production field guide: each root frame is an approved pose with slate, scene/episode/model boxes and an APPROVED stamp box.
notes: Honest label: this file is a pose sheet, not a staged scene — 2 root frames, no background. The performance poses live in the puppet timelines inside the FLA.
Angle-specific puppets (top shot here) are a standing technique in this production: new viewpoint = new puppet variant, not a transform trick.
The field-guide frame (4/3 SAFE / FULL guides, CN bug, slate) is part of every GB209 export — presentation and approval are built into the file.
